title: Merge upstream's newest code (5.0.1 and later) and keep the timeline export and -w working
description:
Step 2 of the upstream sync (step 1, PR #2, is merged into develop as 949ce54f). Bring this fork's develop up to upstream ReagentX/imessage-exporter develop at the PINNED commit 47b75148 (tag 5.0.1 plus 18 commits; "Merge pull request #870 ... business-leave"). Justin's request (June 2026): "Please pull the changes from the upstream repo and reconcile."

## In scope
- One real merge commit of 47b75148 into branch worktree-upstream-5-sync (no squash, no rebase, no cherry-pick), so future syncs stay clean.
- Resolve the 5 conflicting files: imessage-exporter/src/app/options.rs, imessage-exporter/src/exporters/html/resources/style.css, imessage-exporter/Cargo.toml, imessage-exporter/README.md, docs/tables/duplicates.md.
- Fix compile errors and test failures in FORK-OWNED code caused by upstream API drift.
- Fix the -w exit code bug in imessage-exporter/src/main.rs (fork-owned): when resolve_filtered_handles() returns Err, the program prints "Unable to export" but returns ExitCode::SUCCESS. It must return ExitCode::FAILURE. Add or update a test if the code shape allows one; if not, the smoke test below is the proof.
- Stop the fork's formatter from rewriting upstream-owned files: add upstream-owned paths to .prettierignore (at least imessage-database/, imessage-exporter/, docs/, README.md, .github/) so the pre-commit hook (lint-staged runs `prettier --write` on staged *.md/*.json/*.yml) and `bun run signal` leave them alone.
- Revert the fork's past formatting-only churn in upstream-owned files to upstream's exact text at 47b75148 (e.g. `git checkout 47b75148 -- <file>`). Known churned files: style.css, html/resources/example.html, docs/faq.md, docs/features.md, docs/tables/*.md, README.md, imessage-exporter/README.md (keep only the fork's real timeline / -w additions in imessage-exporter/README.md).

## Fork-owned code (the ONLY places the final tree may differ from 47b75148)
- imessage-exporter/src/exporters/timeline.rs (whole file), and `pub mod timeline;` in exporters/mod.rs
- ExportType::Timeline in imessage-exporter/src/app/export_type.rs
- --conversation-with / -w in imessage-exporter/src/app/options.rs
- resolve_exact_match_chats and the Result-returning resolve_filtered_handles in imessage-exporter/src/app/runtime.rs, plus the Timeline dispatch there
- the Timeline re-export and the -w error handling in imessage-exporter/src/main.rs
- the chrono dependency line in imessage-exporter/Cargo.toml (align its version pin with whatever chrono pin upstream uses in imessage-database, so the lockfile has one chrono) and the matching Cargo.lock lines
- the timeline / -w documentation in imessage-exporter/README.md
- fork tooling outside the Rust crates: .prettierignore, package.json, CLAUDE.md, .claude/, .beads/, justin-sdk files

## Out of scope
- Any change to upstream-owned code beyond what the merge itself brings in. Do NOT fix upstream clippy warnings, upstream tests, or upstream formatting.
- The Full Disk Access message (bead imessage-exporter-djf.3) and richer timeline rendering (bead imessage-exporter-djf.2): later dispatches.
- Pushing, merging into develop, closing beads: the conductor does these.
- Old worktrees and branches (worktree-sync-upstream-develop, claude/unified-timeline-export-oVkvg): leave untouched.
- Never push to or open anything on the `upstream` remote (ReagentX).

## Privacy contract (non-negotiable)
- Never read message content from a real database or its exports. No cat/head/Read/rg-with-output on export files or on chat.db. Only exit codes, file counts and file sizes (`ls | wc -l`, `du`, `rg -c` counts are fine).
- Do not touch ~/Library/Messages at all. Use the existing May 2026 copy at /Users/jhaa/Dev/imessage-exporter/tmp/db-copy/chat.db (with its -wal and -shm). If opening it in place fails because the folder is not writable from the sandbox, copy the three chat.db* files to /tmp/claude-501/imx-test/db/ and use that copy.
- Write every export of the real copy under /tmp/claude-501/imx-test/out-*/ (outside the repo and outside Dropbox). Redirect the program's stdout and stderr to a log file there; look only at the exit code and the last lines of stderr if it fails. Delete the out-* export folders when you have the counts; keep the db copy.
- -w positive tests use the upstream fixture imessage-database/test_data/db/test.db only (it is synthetic test data; reading it is fine). On the real copy, -w is tested only with a name that cannot exist (e.g. `-w 'ZZ No Such Person 0000'`), which must exit non-zero.
acceptance_criteria:
1. HEAD on worktree-upstream-5-sync is a merge commit with 47b75148 as a parent (`git log --format='%h %p' -1` shows it, or a later commit sits on top of such a merge).
2. Tree diff gate: `git diff --stat 47b75148 HEAD -- imessage-database imessage-exporter Cargo.toml Cargo.lock docs README.md .github` lists ONLY fork-owned files from the description. Every other difference is reverted to upstream's text. The player pastes this --stat output in its report.
3. `CARGO_HOME=/tmp/claude-501/cargo-home cargo build --workspace` passes.
4. `CARGO_HOME=/tmp/claude-501/cargo-home cargo test --workspace` passes with 0 failures; the report gives the pass counts per test binary.
5. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` (same CARGO_HOME) shows no warning in a fork-owned file. Warnings in upstream-owned files are listed in the report, not fixed.
6. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes for fork-owned files (if upstream files fail rustfmt, list them, do not fix them).
7. `bun run signal` passes.
8. Release build: `cargo build --release` passes.
9. Smoke tests with the release binary, each recording the exit code (and file counts only):
   a. `-f timeline` on the fixture test.db: exit 0, at least one .md file.
   b. `-f timeline -w <a handle that exists in the fixture>`: exit 0, exactly the matching chat's output (file count).
   c. `-f timeline -w 'ZZ No Such Person 0000'` on the fixture: exit non-zero, stderr names the no-match error.
   d. On the May real-db copy: `-f timeline`, `-f txt`, `-f html` each exit 0 with a non-zero file count (attachments off: default copy-method).
   e. On the May real-db copy: `-f timeline -w 'ZZ No Such Person 0000'` exits non-zero.
10. Negative control for the exit-code fix: with the fix temporarily reverted, smoke test (c) exits 0; restored, it exits non-zero.
11. All work committed on worktree-upstream-5-sync; working tree clean except git-ignored paths.

title: Which imessage-exporter work should I build before the 3 pm reset?
description:
Form: pick
Header: Pick work

Context:
- Your open beads hold four items from June. One is already done (PR #1, the Markdown timeline export, is merged). One is obsolete: both clippy warnings sit in code that upstream has since rewritten. That leaves the three options below.
- Option a evidence: on 2026-06-07 you wrote 'There's been a lot of progress it looks like on this since I forked. Please pull the changes from the upstream repo and reconcile.' A session merged 285 upstream commits and opened PR #2, but PR #2 was never merged. Upstream has since added 217 more commits and released 4.2, 4.3 and 5.0.1.
- Option a plan, step 1: build PR #2 on today's Rust and run its tests, then merge it into develop (this fork's main branch). A dry-run merge into develop shows no conflicts. Step 2: merge the 217 newer upstream commits, fix 5 conflicting files (2 real: the CLI options file and the HTML stylesheet), and re-check the timeline export and -w against upstream 5.0. Step 2 may still be in progress at 3 pm.
- Option b evidence: on 2026-05-10 you wrote 'I don't think the issue is full disk access -- I can access the chat.db file from the terminal.' The cause was that macOS checks the built binary itself, not the terminal. The message still says to give your terminal Full Disk Access, in this fork and in upstream today.
- Option c evidence is weaker: a Claude session wrote this bead on 2026-06-07 when you asked it to 'file beads for the remaining items'. Your own words never named link previews or music. Today the timeline export prints '[App message]' for link previews, Apple Music shares, polls and similar messages.
- Safety: players test only on the repo's test fixtures and on a copy of chat.db inside the repo's tmp folder (git-ignored and in your Dropbox ignore list). They check exit codes and file counts only, and never read message text, so no message content goes to the model or off this Mac.
- How you test option a: copy the database with cp ~/Library/Messages/chat.db* /tmp/imx/ and run the new binary with -p /tmp/imx/chat.db -f timeline -w on one contact. I will give exact commands when it is built. Your daily imessage-exporter is still Homebrew 3.3.2 from February, which has no timeline format.

Options:
a. (Recommended) Land the upstream sync: merge PR #2 now, then bring in upstream 5.0.1. Upside: finishes your June request and picks up 5 months of upstream fixes. Downside: biggest change, about 60 to 75 minutes, and step 2 may not finish before 3 pm.
b. Fix the Full Disk Access error message: name the binary path to add, and suggest -p with a copied database. Upside: about 15 minutes, fixes the exact confusion you hit. Downside: small. Best done after option a, because upstream rewrote that file.
c. Render link previews, music and polls in the timeline export instead of [App message]. Upside: richer exports. Downside: about 45 to 60 minutes, depends on option a landing first, and the evidence you want it is weak. I would not start it before 3 pm.

No default: the session stops here
